q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of pickles per kg?
title: Pickle carbon footprint per kg
short: Add the vegetables or fruit, edible oil, salt and spices from supplier or database factors, then cutting, cooking and filling energy, and the glass jar or pouch. Divide by kilograms packed. Oil and the jar are often bigger than the plant's own energy.

ul: Raw mango, lime, chilli or mixed vegetables, counted by weight bought, including peel and stones discarded.
Mustard or sesame oil: vegetable oils carry a sizeable farm footprint per kg.
Electricity for cutters, mixers and filling lines.
LPG or PNG for heating oil and tempering spices.

p: A glass jar can weigh more than the pickle inside a small pack, and glass is energy-intensive. Compare jar against PET or pouch per kg of product, and include caps and labels.

example.title: Worked example: pickle unit per kg (one month)
lines: Cooking LPG: 800 kg x 2.98 = 2,384 kg CO2
Plant total: 5,934 / 40,000 = 0.148 kg CO2 per kg
Add produce, oil, spices and jars for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
